description: A campaign file is the only interface for defining what a campaign does (ADR-0016). Every field is optional in the schema; what is actually required is reported by `xfuzz validate`, which can say things a schema cannot — that a target path is executable, that a scope is present when the campaign leaves the host, that a grammar exists.

extensions.description: Out-of-process plugins and the extension points each supplies.

batch.description: Variants a plugin mutator produces per call.

config.description: Settings handed to the plugin at startup.

feedbacks.description: Feedbacks to take from this plugin.

input.description: Send the executed bytes to this plugin.

mutators.description: Mutators to take from this plugin.

name.description: Label for this plugin, used to qualify its extensions.

objectives.description: Objectives to take from this plugin.

timeout.description: Bound on one call to the plugin.

cmplog.description: Substitute the target's own comparison operands into the input.

coverage.description: Coverage backend: sancov, ptrace-bb, qemu, frida, blackbox, or none.

directed.description: Aim the campaign at particular locations in the target.

min_reachable.description: Refuse to start if less than this fraction of blocks can reach a target.

targets.description: Where to aim: a function name, file.c:123, or 0xADDRESS.

weight.description: How much the schedule favours seeds closer to the target.

objectives.description: What counts as a finding: crash, hang, oom, sanitizer.

value_profile.description: Treat getting closer to passing a comparison as new coverage.

format.description: How bytes are interpreted as structure.

suppress.description: Derivations to leave inconsistent: length, count, offset, checksum.

health.description: Thresholds the health diagnostics judge against.

coverage_stall.description: How long without new coverage counts as stalled. Default 30m.

max_overhead.description: Share of time the fuzzer may spend on itself. Default 0.10.

min_execs_per_second.description: Rate below which the executor is judged broken. Default 10.

min_stability.description: Share of executions that must reproduce their coverage. Default 0.90.

include.description: Files merged in before this one, in order.

mutation.description: Which operators run and how they are weighted.

operators.description: Operator names to enable. Empty enables all.

trim_budget.description: Executions spent trimming each new corpus entry. 0 disables.

name.description: Campaign name, unique within a store.

profiles.description: Named overlays, applied on top when selected.

safety.description: Isolation, resource limits, network scope, authorization.

authorization.description: Who authorised this campaign, and under what reference.

attestation.description: Statement that the operator is authorised to test the declared scope.

reference.description: Engagement identifier, ticket, or approval reference.

file_size_limit.description: Largest file the target may write.

isolation.description: Minimum isolation level: none, minimal, moderate, strong.

network.description: Leave the target in the host network namespace.

scope.description: Network allowlist for campaigns that leave the host.

acknowledge_public.description: Acknowledge that the scope reaches public address space.

allow.description: Allowed destinations: host, address, or CIDR, optionally with :ports.

writable.description: Extra writable paths under the read-only root.

scripts.description: Campaign-local Starlark and the extension points each supplies.

batch.description: Variants a script mutator produces per call.

config.description: Settings the script reads as config.

mutators.description: Mutator functions to take from this script.

name.description: Label for this script, used to qualify its extensions.

objectives.description: Oracle functions to take from this script.

steps.description: Computation steps one call may take.

seed.description: Root RNG seed. Absent draws one; pinning it makes the campaign reproducible.

seeds.description: Where the starting corpus comes from.

format.description: Corpus layout: auto, afl, libfuzzer, or raw.

generate.description: Seeds to generate from the grammar when no corpus is given.

max_file_size.description: Largest seed file to import, in bytes.

session.description: Protocol sessions: where the target listens, how replies are framed, and what resets between sessions.

address.description: Where the target listens: tcp:HOST:PORT or unix:PATH. {worker} is replaced with the worker index.

framing.description: When a reply is complete: idle, line, or none.

managed.description: Start the target process. Defaults to true when target.path is set.

quiet_period.description: How long idle framing waits before a reply is complete.

read_limit.description: Maximum bytes retained from one reply.

reset.description: Between sessions: none, reconnect, restart, or snapshot.

state.description: The protocol state machine, declared or inferred, and how it guides the campaign.

declare.description: Declared transitions as "from->to". Moves outside them are reported.

explore.description: How often to aim for a rare state, 0..1.

fn.description: How a response becomes a state label: status, http, fingerprint, or constant.

guide.description: Treat new states and transitions as interesting. Defaults to true.

normalise.description: What fingerprinting removes before hashing: digits, quoted, space.

script.description: Starlark state function as NAME:FUNCTION, when fn is script.

tail_bias.description: How often an aimed mutation lands at or after the target state, 0..1.

stop.description: Termination conditions. A campaign must be able to end.

findings.description: Stop after this many distinct finding buckets.

no_new_coverage.description: Stop after this long without new coverage.

storage.description: Where the corpus and findings live, and their budgets.

checkpoint_interval.description: How often resume state is written.

dir.description: Store directory. Empty uses the daemon's data directory.

max_corpus_bytes.description: Corpus size cap in bytes. 0 is unlimited.

target.description: What to fuzz and how to deliver input to it.

args.description: Arguments after the program name. @@ is replaced with the input file path.

executor.description: Delivery tier: auto, forkserver, pool, subprocess, inproc, or emulated.

input.description: How input is delivered: stdin, file, or arg.

triage.description: How findings are verified, minimised, and bucketed.

markers.description: Extra line prefixes that name a failure in the target's own words.

strategy.description: Bucketing strategy: chain, frames, marker, coverage, or signal.

workers.description: How many workers and what strategies they run.

count.description: Worker processes. 0 means one per core.

mutation.description: Mutation overrides for workers running this strategy.

operators.description: Operator names to enable. Empty enables all.

trim_budget.description: Executions spent trimming each new corpus entry. 0 disables.

schedule.description: Power schedule: fast, rand, or roundrobin.

sync_interval.description: How often workers exchange corpus entries.

title: Xfuzz campaign
